We're preparing for a regulatory evidence request and need to understand Redwood's capabilities for delivering tenant audit/access logs. A few specific asks:

- Proof of deletion / certificate after user-requested erasure: what does Redwood provide?
- How does legal hold interact with scheduled deletion windows?

Can you send a short runbook or checklist we can include with our evidence package? Thanks — we have a tight deadline next week.

Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention & export options

Hi all — technical answers below; I attached a short spec (export_spec.xlsx) and runbook (export_runbook.pdf) for your reviewers.

1) Retention windows
- Default tenant retention is 90 days for high-volume audit traces.
- We offer configurable retention tiers up to 7 years for audit/access logs as a paid option (reserved capacity / enterprise).
- Regional constraints: EU tenants can be configured to store and export within eu-west-1 only. US/Global tenants have cross-region export options (subject to export approvals).

2) Bulk exports / formats
- Point-in-time exports by date range are supported; typical export granularity is hourly slices aggregated into date-range bundles.
- Supported output formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) and Parquet. We can also provide gzipped CSV for lightweight ingestion.

3) Delivery methods
- Preferred standard: S3 presigned URL (time-limited, HTTPS) to a customer bucket. We can push to a customer S3 account with IAM role assumption if required.
- Alternate: Encrypted tarball delivered via secure transfer (signed URL) to a provider-managed bucket and then shared with the customer.
- All exports are server-side encrypted. We support customer-managed KMS keys (CMK) for S3 deliveries where PKI/keys are required.

4) Manifest, integrity, and chain-of-custody
- Each export includes a manifest JSON (sample_manifest.ndjson attached) with: export_id, tenant_id, time_range, file_list, SHA256 checksums, and a signed export_token.
- We can provide SHA256 sums and a simple signed statement indicating the files were generated from the tenant's live audit store at the stated time.

5) Deletion & proof of deletion
- Standard deletion: when a retention window lapses, records enter a tombstone state and are physically deleted within our erase pipeline (up to 30 days for cold archive purges).
- On customer-initiated erasure (subject to legal holds), we provide a deletion certificate describing scope, time, and method. For high-assurance cases we can provide: deleted_export_manifest (list of deleted object keys + checksum) and timestamped audit event showing erase operation.

6) Legal hold interaction
- When legal hold is applied at tenant level, scheduled deletions are suspended for the affected data classes. Holds must be requested via our evidence intake process; we provide a hold_id and can include hold metadata in export manifests.

7) SLA & timing
- Typical export for a single tenant date-range (<= 6 months) completes within 24–72 hours depending on size. For larger archives (multi-year) we provide a scoped timeline during intake. Emergency evidence exports can be escalated via our incident channel.

Attachments: export_spec.xlsx, export_runbook.pdf, sample_manifest.ndjson

Happy to walk through these in a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Lara — quick legal notes to help your evidence package language:

- Attestation vs. Certification: we can provide factual export statements (what was exported, when, and how) and a deletion certificate. We do not provide legal certifications or opinions on behalf of your counsel.
- Wording suggestion for evidence: "Redwood Inference provided a point-in-time export for tenant XYZ covering 2025-01-01 to 2026-12-31. Export files and manifest were delivered to FinServCorp via S3 presigned URL. Checksums and export_id: <id> are included in the manifest."
- Legal holds: must reference the hold_id we issue to you; it is the authoritative identifier for suspension of deletions.
- Chain-of-custody: if you require notarized chain-of-custody, we will need to engage our legal ops team (additional lead time).

If you want, Vanessa can coordinate a short statement template that matches your regulator's expectations.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
